reproduction_target: No computational reproduction target. The paper is an experimental cardiovascular study (human HLHS myocardium, HLHS-iPSC-derived cardiomyocytes, neonatal/immature rat ischemia-reperfusion) using qRT-PCR, Western blot, transmission electron microscopy, echocardiography, Langendorff perfusion and LDH assay. The only computational artifact is group-comparison statistics performed in the GraphPad Prism 10 GUI. There is no sequencing, no omics analysis, no pipeline, and no analysis code. Documentation-audit only per guide Step 0 (pure-wet-lab route).
granularity_note: No workflow file exists (no code repository is stated). Steps derived from the Methods section of the bioRxiv JATS XML, one step per named assay/tool invocation. Main-text Methods are abbreviated: 'A detailed description of the methods and materials can be found in the Supplemental Material.' The Supplemental Materials and Methods were NOT retrieved (separate supplementary file, not present in the JATS source XML), so the step list reflects the main-text Methods only; step count could grow modestly if the supplement names additional software (e.g. densitometry or image-analysis packages). Scope-split yields |S|=1 computational step and |W|=11 wet-lab (OOS) steps.

steps.label: Group-comparison statistics (Student's t-test, one-way ANOVA, two-way ANOVA) in GraphPad Prism 10
Human heart tissue collection and processing (6 HLHS patients aged 3-12 months at transplantation; donor-heart controls; IRB-approved discarded specimens)
HLHS-iPSC culture (Essential 8 medium, 1:4 passage) and cardiomyocyte differentiation/purification; lines purchased from Stanford University
shRNA-H19 lentiviral transduction of HLHS-iPSC-CMs and hypoxia/reoxygenation injury (HRI) model
Intracardiac lentiviral vector injection in 2-3 day-old Wistar rats (2 x 10^12 particles; shRNA-H19/PINK1/Parkin vs scrambled) under VisualSonics echocardiographic guidance
In vivo myocardial IRI in 14-15 day-old rats (60 min LAD occlusion, 24 h reperfusion) with TTC infarct staining and phthalocyanine blue area-at-risk delineation
Ex vivo Langendorff retrograde perfusion (80 mmHg, Krebs-Henseleit, 37 C; 30 min stabilization, 60 min global ischemia, 120 min reperfusion) with LV hemodynamics (LVDP, +dP/dt, -dP/dt)
Transthoracic echocardiography (VisualSonics Vevo 3100) for ejection fraction, LVIDd/LVIDs, fractional shortening over 28 days
Transmission electron microscopy (60-70 nm ultrathin sections, uranyl acetate/lead citrate, Philips CM120 at 60 kV) and manual mitophagosome quantification
qRT-PCR of H19, PINK1 and Parkin (miScript RT mix, SYBR Green, Rnu-6 housekeeping; human and rat H19 primer sequences given verbatim)
Western blot and densitometry of PINK1/Parkin in whole lysates and isolated mitochondrial fractions (GAPDH, beta-actin, GTPCH loading controls); densitometry software not named
Lactate dehydrogenase (LDH) release assay in HLHS-iPSC-CMs using LDH Assay Kit

headline.static_readiness: 0/1 (0%) - stage1 ceiling only, no R-star (R-star needs stage-2 code verification). Unexecuted; declared environment statically valid but not verified as the env that produced the results. Co-reported: n_exact_capture_unexecuted=0, n_fetch_required=0. has_validated_env_capture=false, so this per-paper ratio is a ceiling artefact and must not be quoted as a paper-level score (P2). It also under-claims by construction - Tier-1 cannot credit an undeclared-but-present dependency.
headline.inference_inclusive_upper_bound: (n_R + n_RI)/|S| = 0/1 (0%) - readiness upper bound, never 'reproducible'. The single C-step is NI: source data are author-request-only and no analysis script exists.
headline.coverage: computational coverage |S|/(|S|+|W|) = 1/12 (8%). Pure-wet-lab paper: 11 of 12 steps are OOS bench/animal/imaging work. The lone C-step is GUI statistics in a commercial package. Denominator |S|=1 is far below the ReproIndex refusal threshold (|S|<4), so repro_index is null and no within-paper ratio may be used for cross-paper ranking (guide section 10 firewall).

gaps.where: Whole paper - no Code Availability statement exists
gaps.missing: No code repository of any kind (GitHub/GitLab/Bitbucket/Zenodo/Software Heritage) is stated anywhere in the article. There is no Code Availability section; the only availability statement is the Data Availability statement under METHODS.
gaps.how_to_close: Deposit the statistical analysis (Prism project files or an equivalent R/Python script reproducing the reported tests) plus per-figure source data in a citable archive (Zenodo DOI) and cite it in a Code Availability section.

gaps.missing: No analysis code is private-or-public: the analysis is a GUI workflow in GraphPad Prism 10, so no executable artefact exists to deposit or inspect.
gaps.how_to_close: Export the Prism project file (.pzfx) alongside the underlying tidy data table, or re-implement the reported tests as a short script.

gaps.missing: No per-sample source data. Verbatim: 'The data that support the findings of this study are available from the corresponding author on reasonable request.' No accession (GEO/SRA/ENA/ArrayExpress/dbGaP/EGA/figshare/Zenodo), no repository, no per-figure numeric source-data file. Figure legends give group n (n=4-15 per group) but the individual measurements underlying every bar/scatter are not deposited.
gaps.how_to_close: Deposit de-identified per-figure numeric source data (densitometry ratios, mitophagosome counts per field, hemodynamic traces, echocardiographic measurements, delta-Ct values) in a repository with a DOI. Human tissue data may legitimately use a controlled-access route with a documented DAC path (that would score Data=2 under the rubric); author-request-only does not.

gaps.missing: GraphPad Prism 10 is proprietary commercial software. Under guide Step 4 this is license-gated; under the Step-8 ceiling, proprietary dependency caps the step at NI.
gaps.how_to_close: Nothing is required of the authors beyond depositing the source data; a reader without a Prism licence can re-run the described tests in any statistics package if the tidy data are available.

gaps.where: Statistics (step C1) - 'Statistical analyses were conducted using GraphPad Prism 10.'
gaps.missing: Major-version line only ('Prism 10'), no point release (e.g. 10.4.1), no OS/platform, no environment closure. Scored version=1 as license-gated; version_subtier=floating because a major line is a mutable target, not an exact pin.
gaps.how_to_close: State the exact Prism build and the operating system, or move the statistics to a scripted environment with a lockfile.

gaps.where: Western blot densitometry (step W10) and mitophagosome quantification (step W8)
gaps.missing: The software used for band densitometry and for TEM image measurement is not named at all in the main-text Methods. If a named image-analysis tool exists it would be a further C-step; it may appear in the unretrieved Supplemental Materials and Methods.
gaps.how_to_close: Name the densitometry/image-analysis software and version, and state the quantification settings (background subtraction, ROI definition, blinding, fields per sample).

gaps.missing: 11 of 12 steps are non-computational wet-lab / animal / imaging procedures and are out of scope for NASEM-2019 computational reproducibility. This is the dominant characteristic of the paper, not a defect.
gaps.how_to_close: N/A - OOS by routing. Wet-lab protocol reproducibility would be assessed under a different instrument (e.g. protocols.io deposition), not this rubric.
